title: When the Tryouts Turns
premise: Juniper Brightwater has spent four years holding her family together while her mother works graveyard shifts, treating graduation as the finish line of a sentence she never chose. When her civics teacher pairs her with Theo Vance — the school board chair's son and her longtime nemesis — on a semester project about local government, they stumble into sealed records showing the district quietly sold the land beneath the community center where Juniper's siblings spend their afternoons. As eviction notices loom and someone starts erasing documents, Juniper and Theo must decide whether to trust each other, expose the cover-up through channels that don't exist yet, and learn that justice sometimes has to be built by hand. The book ends at a raucous board meeting where Juniper's testimony, backed by recovered records and an unlikely coalition of students and neighbors, forces the sale's reversal — and she finally sees graduation not as escape, but as a beginning.
about_author: Emrys Nakamura grew up in a rust-belt town where the high school gym doubled as the polling place, and learned early how budgets get buried in plain sight. A former debate coach and night-shift barista, Nakamura writes stories about kids who do the math adults refuse to.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV opens on a Tuesday: packing lunches, waking her brother Milo and sister Dee, then surviving homeroom where a countdown calendar marks days to graduation. She frames her life as a sentence being served. Emotional beat: weary competence masking exhaustion, and a fierce love for her siblings.

chapters.title: The Assignment
chapters.summary: Civics teacher Ms. Okafor announces semester-long partnerships for a 'Local Power' project and reads names aloud: Brightwater and Vance. Juniper's POV; the classroom goes quiet because everyone knows these two are oil and water. Beat: dread sharpening into defiance as she refuses to let Theo sink her GPA.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Juniper and Theo negotiate ground rules in the library, all barbed politeness. His father chairs the school board; he assumes she'll slack. Her POV reveals why she can't afford anything less than an A. Beat: grudging truce signed in borrowed pencil.

chapters.title: What the Center Means
chapters.summary: Juniper brings the project to the Riverside Community Center where Milo does homework after school, showing Theo the mural her late grandmother painted. His POV softens as he watches her translate bureaucracy into people. Beat: first crack in the nemesis armor.

chapters.title: Redacted
chapters.summary: Researching land transfers at the county archive, they find the parcel file for the center — pages missing, a stamp reading 'sealed by board action.' Alternating POV. Beat: curiosity curdling into suspicion when a clerk hurries them out mid-question.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Hours
chapters.summary: Juniper's home life strains: mom picks up extra shifts, Dee acts out, and Juniper misses a study session. Theo shows up unasked with pizza and flashcards for Milo. Her POV. Beat: resentment of help warring with gratitude — belonging offered, not owed.

chapters.title: Follow the Money
chapters.summary: Theo pulls his father's old campaign filings and finds a donor connected to a development firm bidding on riverfront parcels. His POV, terrified of what his own name implies. Beat: loyalty to family colliding with an emerging conscience.

chapters.title: The Whistle in the Stacks
chapters.summary: An anonymous note appears in Juniper's locker: 'Ask about Resolution 41.' They trace it to a retired board secretary, Ruth Ibarra, who hints at a vote taken without public notice. Juniper's POV. Beat: the thrill of a real lead and the fear of what asking costs.

chapters.title: Ruth's Box
chapters.summary: In Ruth's garage, they find a box of duplicates: minutes, appraisals, and a memo valuing the center's land at a fraction of market rate before the sale. Theo's POV, hands shaking. Beat: proof is real, and so is the danger — Ruth warns them someone came asking last month.

chapters.title: Eviction Notice
chapters.summary: The center receives thirty days' notice of 'structural review,' transparently pretextual. Juniper's POV as Milo asks if the mural will be torn down. Beat: abstract injustice becomes a clock ticking over her brother's head.

chapters.title: Allies and Alibis
chapters.summary: They recruit classmates: Priya the journalist, Marcus the coder, Dee's art club. Theo lies to his father about a study group. Alternating POV. Beat: a ragtag coalition forms, and Juniper feels, for once, not alone but responsible for others.

chapters.title: The Father-Son Fault Line
chapters.summary: Theo confronts his father at dinner; the conversation turns glacial, and his access to the house — and his college fund — is threatened. His POV. Beat: the true cost of inheritance: he can keep the name or the truth, not both.

chapters.title: Shredded
chapters.summary: Someone breaks into Ruth's garage; the box is gone, and Ruth lands in the hospital after a fall she swears wasn't one. Juniper's POV, guilt and fury braided together. Beat: the stakes turn physical; this is no longer a class project.

chapters.title: Backup Everything
chapters.summary: Marcus reveals he scanned everything weeks ago; relief, then a new problem — the scans need authentication, and the only witness who can verify them is hospitalized and scared. Theo's POV. Beat: hope rekindled, tempered by Ruth's whispered refusal to testify.

chapters.title: The Deal Offered
chapters.summary: A district lawyer offers Juniper a quiet scholarship and a transfer if the project 'pivots topics.' Her POV, tempted — it would solve money problems forever. Beat: the seduction of exit versus the pull of belonging; she declines, barely.

chapters.title: Dee's Mural March
chapters.summary: Dee organizes kids to chalk the center's parking lot with the mural's images and facts from the case; the story hits local news. Juniper's POV watching her sister become brave in ways she never modeled. Beat: the movement outgrows its founders.

chapters.title: Resolution 41, Found
chapters.summary: Priya's FOIA request surfaces a misfiled copy of Resolution 41 with signatures — including Theo's father's. His POV as he decides to hand it to the group himself. Beat: betrayal of blood for principle, done with steady hands and a breaking heart.

chapters.title: Sabotage
chapters.summary: Days before the board meeting, the school accuses Juniper of plagiarism in the project and suspends her pending review; her graduation is threatened. Her POV at the lowest point. Beat: the system strikes back personally, and she nearly believes she deserves it.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: Juniper speaks at the packed board meeting anyway, suspended or not, flanked by Ruth — who arrives in a wheelchair, ready to authenticate the records. Alternating POV. Climax beat: her voice steadies as she names every signature, ending on the mural: 'You're not selling land. You're selling us.'

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: Under public pressure and a state inquiry triggered by Priya's reporting, the board rescinds the sale and voids Resolution 41; Theo's father resigns. Theo's POV watching his mother's face. Beat: justice outside the law's normal speed, won by ordinary people refusing to leave.

chapters.title: Aftermaths
chapters.summary: Suspension lifted, plagiarism charge dropped; Theo and Juniper present the project to a standing ovation they barely hear. Quiet scene at the center, repainting scuffed mural edges, Ruth telling stories. Juniper's POV. Beat: tenderness after battle; nemesis becomes something unnamed and warm.

chapters.title: Graduation Day
chapters.summary: Juniper walks across the stage with Milo and Dee screaming her name, mom front row having swapped shifts one last time. Final POV shift between Juniper and Theo exchanging a look across the gym. Closing beat: the sentence served becomes a sentence begun — she's staying, building, belonging.
